03 · KIWI BUZZUX/UI · Service Access · App Redesign

Making temporary access easier to follow.

KIWI Buzz explores a clearer mobile experience for technicians requesting and using temporary access to residential buildings.

Role
UX Designer
Project
Academic redesign project
Context
KIWI
Focus
Temporary building access

The challenge

Access shouldn’t feel complicated.

The project focused on technicians who need temporary, time-limited access to specific areas of a residential building. The presentation identifies a time-consuming journey across the app store, email, phone and app. The redesign explores bringing the request and access steps into one guided mobile experience.

The journey

Making the steps easier to understand.

The documented journey starts at the building door and continues through the access request to unlocking.

  1. Arrive

    Reach the building door and find the QR poster.

  2. Scan & download

    Scan the QR code, open the app store and download the app.

  3. Request

    Fill in the required information.

  4. Wait for confirmation

    The request is reviewed before access is granted.

  5. Open the door

    Use the granted access to open the door via Bluetooth.

Structuring the experience

From flow to interface.

The wireframes helped translate the access journey into a clearer sequence of screens before moving into the final visual interface.

Final interface

A clearer path to access.

The final interface brings the main access steps into one consistent mobile experience, helping technicians understand where they are in the process and what action comes next.

Access & permissions

See what’s available.
Find the right door.

The building view groups doors by floor, while Active Keys brings currently available access into a focused list.

Unlocking

One door.
One clear action.

The selected door stays visible alongside a direct instruction to place the phone near it. The unlock action becomes the focus of the screen.

What changed in the experience.

01

A guided request

Reason for visit and identification appear together, followed by a dedicated review state.

02

Visible access status

The waiting message, floor tabs and Active Keys view make different parts of the access process explicit.

03

A focused unlock action

The final door screen centres the selected door and a single prominent Unlock control.

Reflection

What I took from it.

This project made me think more carefully about designing around a sequence of actions rather than individual screens. Mapping the access journey first helped me understand how each step connects, and how small interface decisions can make a process easier to follow.
